reference: Runnable expectations use documented Bash type/help builtin behavior and the dmsetup builtin's published help contract; expected sentinels are fixed in this suite and do not come from candidate output. Device-mapper operation expectations are deferred for comparison against the LVM2 dmsetup CLI and an independently decoded Linux Device Mapper ioctl model in a future disposable VM or reviewed mock.
coverage: Bash reports dmsetup as a builtin using both type -t and type descriptions.
Bash help metadata exposes the documented dmsetup description, command families, and mutation opt-in requirement.
Deferred plans cover query output, table input and loading, state changes, removal, rename and messages, and ioctl/error behavior.
Metadata only; operation coverage is zero. Deferred cases are future qualification requirements.
exclusions: No dmsetup operation is invoked: queries and mutations communicate with the kernel device-mapper control interface, and mutations can alter block-device state.
Real device behavior, target-specific message handling, udev coordination, and open-device removal require a disposable VM or reviewed ioctl mock.
There is no runnable parity oracle for the loadable's metadata in system Bash, which does not register this custom builtin.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t must identify the registered dmsetup command as a builtin.
Bash type must describe dmsetup as a shell builtin, matching its documented command registration.
The -d help view must expose the documented short description for dmsetup.
cases.stdout: dmsetup short help description is present

cases.purpose: Full help must include the documented query and mutation command families and the explicit mutation opt-in policy.
cases.stdout: dmsetup help synopsis and policy are present

cases.purpose: Compare empty and populated ls/info results, name and UUID lookup, device state, and no-device behavior.
cases.reason: Every device-mapper ioctl checks CAP_SYS_ADMIN (drivers/md/dm-ioctl.c ctl_ioctl returns -EACCES otherwise) and /dev/mapper/control is root 0600, so uid 2000 cannot create, query or observe mapped devices; the candidate additionally refuses mutations unless euid 0 and BASHOS_DMSETUP_ALLOW_MUTATE=1 (dmsetup.c:926-932, gate at :1477) before opening the control node. r5 needs no privilege and no new driver.
